findings.reason: the section must name a second, write-capable node (or split into census and apply sections), otherwise the whole write half of §49 has no dispatchable identity.
findings.text: §49 names exactly one node, `sib-separatrix-locus-census`, described as "a read-only census", but its done-when closes the section on three further deliverables it does not name a node for: a lead ruling on the mapping, the ruled renames and supersedes applied through signed paths, and the tritium retire-and-compose. A dispatcher can dispatch the census and then has no node id to close the section with, which is precisely the shape §48 needed two nodes (`sib-rebind-removed-path-names`, `sib-magnetic-successor-edge`) to satisfy.

findings.reason: a census author following the section as written will either stop at a read-only deliverable or supersede onto a dead holder, and the section's own rule forbids reviving a tombstone.
findings.text: the mechanism §49 describes is "a read-only census"; the done-when it must satisfy asserts that the "ruled renames and supersedes, and the tritium retire-and-compose, are applied through signed paths, with a live read-back". A read-only node cannot apply anything, so the section's own mechanism cannot produce its own measure. Separately, the example it gives for a tombstone's live successor — `electron_temperature_at_plasma_boundary` "to `bulk_electron_temperature_at_plasma_boundary`" — is contradicted by `docs/evidence/fragments/sn-integrity-backlog/sib-catalog-import-source-census.json` (`non_carried[18]`), which records `bulk_electron_temperature_at_plasma_boundary` as `"status": "superseded"`, `"stage": "superseded"`, `"in_catalog": false`, i.e. itself a tombstone; the same file records `electron_temperature_at_plasma_boundary` as `"in_catalog": true` and superseded.

findings.reason: without a named name that must remain unchanged and a red-at-base assertion for at least one rename, the section's gate cannot show its guard fires and a swap that overshoots its population reads as success.
findings.text: §49's done-when has no negative control and no base arm. "A live read-back showing one suffix per DD locus" states neither the locus set nor a floor on how many names must change, and nothing in the section makes a name that must stay put observable, so the read-back is satisfied by whatever the write step happened to do; the other bullets (fragment exists, lead ruled, spend ≤ USD 2) hold on an unfixed tree.

findings.reason: a recorded reversal of a lead ruling with no evidence path cannot be re-checked when the census disagrees with it, and this review could not confirm two of the three corrections from the repository.
findings.text: the three corrections that overturn the lead's fold ruling — "four of its five targets are superseded tombstones", "the DD has two loci", and "there are 9 live `_at_separatrix` names, not 5" — are attributed to "A coordinator read before acting" and cite no fragment, JSON, commit or run path. The only merge the section cites, `38648dee7`, is the compose-five-stubs evidence and resolves, but it does not carry these readings; the two-loci claim does resolve against `imas_codex/resources/imas_data_dictionary/4.1.1/mappings/path_mappings.json`, and the "live successor" reading does not resolve (see the reasoning finding).

findings.reason: §48 now delivers no work to a node, so an imprecise measure on a closed section cannot direct a dispatch; the change that matters would be to §49, not to this text.
findings.text: the `_document` change flips `s48` to `done` while its done-when still reads "the four rebound names each have exactly one non-stale producing source per row above" against a row that carries two removed paths and the action "rebind both"; the s48 close comment records both `current_tor` paths rebound to `current_phi`, so the work resolves the ambiguity the wording leaves.

rubric_items.anchors_resolve: a finding — the three corrections that overturn the lead's fold ruling are attributed to "a coordinator read before acting" with no evidence path, so a later reader cannot open the reading they rest on.
rubric_items.done_when: a finding — §49's done-when declares no negative control and no base-state reading, and its write phase has no named measure for a name that must NOT move; §48's done-when still carries the "four … per row above" phrasing the earlier review flagged, but §48 is now declared done so it no longer directs a dispatch.
rubric_items.evidence_paths: pass — the done-when requires "the census fragment and JSON", and every sibling node in this plan writes those under `docs/evidence/fragments/sn-integrity-backlog/<node>.html` and `.json`, which is durable; no session scratchpad is named.
rubric_items.naming: pass — §49 is prose only; no plan labels, stage names or ticket numbers reach a symbol, filename or comment, and the section title states the mechanism.
rubric_items.reasoning: a finding — §49's stated mechanism is a read-only census, which cannot produce the "ruled renames and supersedes … applied" that the same section's done-when measures, and its one worked example of a live successor is contradicted by the repository's own catalog census.
rubric_items.single_goal: a finding — §49 names one read-only node (`sib-separatrix-locus-census`) while its done-when closes on a lead ruling plus three classes of write.
rubric_items.wiring: pass — §49 declares no `depends-on` and that is defensible: its population is live graph state and the compose evidence it rests on (`38648dee7`, `be0d2485`, `ceaba7b1`) has already landed, so no declared relationship points at a node that does not exist.
